title: GitLab CI/CD pipeline security
description: For a project built with GitLab CI/CD: protected variables, pinned includes and images, short-lived cloud credentials, job token scope and protected environments.

sources.title: GitLab, OpenID Connect (OIDC) authentication using ID tokens

rules.instruction: Mark CI/CD variables that hold deployment credentials as protected and masked, so only pipelines on protected branches or tags receive them.
rules.verification: List the project and group variables in the CI/CD settings and check the protected and masked flags of each credential.

rules.instruction: Pin `include:project` to a tag or commit SHA with a fully qualified `ref`, and add `integrity` to each `include:remote`.
rules.verification: Review `.gitlab-ci.yml` and its includes for refs without a pin and remote includes without an integrity hash.

rules.instruction: Reference job images by digest (`image@sha256:...`) or by an immutable version tag approved by the team, never `latest`.
rules.verification: Search `.gitlab-ci.yml` for `image:` entries without a digest or version and for `:latest`.

rules.instruction: Authenticate deployment jobs to cloud providers with `id_tokens` and a role restricted to the project and branch, instead of stored access keys.
rules.verification: Check the deployment jobs for `id_tokens`, and review the cloud trust policy conditions on the token's project and ref claims.

rules.instruction: Keep the CI/CD job token allowlist limited to the projects that need access to this project.
rules.verification: Review the job token allowlist in the project's CI/CD settings and remove entries without an owner.

rules.instruction: Mark production environments as protected and name the roles or groups allowed to deploy.
rules.verification: Check the protected environments settings and run a deployment job as a user outside the allowed list to confirm it is blocked.
